s: A company hosts a VPN in an on-premises data center. Employees currently connect to the VPN to access files in their Windows home directories. Recently, there has been a large growth in the number of employees who work remotely. As a result, bandwidth usage for connections into the data center has begun to reach 100% during business hours. The company must design a solution on AWS that will support the growth of the company's remote workforce, reduce the bandwidth usage for connections into the data center, and reduce operational overhead. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)
o: Create an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway. Mount a volume from the Volume Gateway to the on-premises file server.
Migrate the home directories to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server.
Migrate the home directories to Amazon FSx for Lustre.
Migrate remote users to AWS Client VPN
Create an AWS Direct Connect connection from the on-premises data center to AWS.

w.y: Moving Windows home directories to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server, a managed SMB service with AD integration, takes file traffic out of the data center. AWS Client VPN is a managed, elastic VPN that lets remote users connect directly to AWS. Together they remove the data center bandwidth bottleneck with minimal operations.

o.A: Volume Gateway presents iSCSI block storage on-premises; users would still come through the data center VPN.
o.B: Correct: FSx for Windows File Server is managed SMB storage built for Windows home directories.
o.C: FSx for Lustre is a Linux HPC file system and is not suited to Windows SMB home directories.
o.D: Correct: Client VPN scales automatically and moves remote user connections off the data center link.
o.E: Direct Connect adds capacity to AWS but does not reduce remote-user VPN load on the data center and adds operational work.
